Relative to neutral, this FOMC statement is moderately hawkish: a 25 bp hike to 4.5–4.75%, an explicit expectation of “ongoing increases,” and continued balance-sheet runoff. In Taylor-rule terms, with inflation still above 2% and unemployment low, a restrictive stance is consistent with rule-based prescriptions. The emphasis on policy lags and inflation expectations aligns with inflation-forecast targeting and optimal policy under commitment (Svensson and Woodford, 2003–2004). Operationally, raising interest on reserves to 4.65% and setting the ON RRP at 4.55% reflects post-2008 floor-system control of short rates, while QT and guidance influence the expected path and term premia in line with Cochrane–Piazzesi term-structure evidence. Acknowledging that inflation has “eased somewhat” softens the tone, but the stated vigilance on inflation risks keeps the bias toward further tightening.
